newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AFL AUSTRALIAN RULES FOOTBALL-Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.
newsitem.headline: AFL AUSTRALIAN RULES FOOTBALL-Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.

text.p: By Andrew Bartram*
A TIPSTER'S TORMENT
Picking a winner in the AFL this season has been a puzzle that has confounded even the greatest prophets.
Tipsters have made judgments on form and fancy and laid their wisdom on the line by gambling on the bounce of a ball that often defies logic.
Let this column add its claim to the complex art of football clairvoyance and suggest that West Coast will give Carlton the blues tonight at Subiaco Oval.
Carlton have won only twice away from Optus Oval this year and while the Eagles have lost twice at home this year the assignment for the Blues is one of football's toughest.
The contest is shaping into a battle of defences and the Eagles have the league's most frugal although the loss of key defender Glen Jakovich will be keenly felt.
MATCH OF THE DAY
Richmond versus Essendon at the MCG on Saturday would normally command match of the day status but, with both teams wallowing in the bottom three, not this time.
The return of Dustin Fletcher and Mark Mercuri should help the Bombers to their first win in almost two months.

The Western Bulldogs go into Saturday's game injury free but they are yet to play at Waverley Park this year and can expect a torrid contest against St Kilda who have won six of their past seven games.
The Bulldogs are the competition leaders but let themselves down badly with an inexplicable last-round loss to Port Adelaide.
The inclusion of the brilliant but wayward Nicky Winmar should give the Saints the edge in a close game.
Fourth placed Geelong hosts second placed Adelaide at Kardinia Park on Saturday.
The Crows are yet to win in five attempts at Geelong where their average losing margin is more than 10 goals.
Normally, such an abysmal record would tell Adelaide's woeful travel tales but the Crows are the best performed road team in the competition this season.
Geelong however, will be well rested after the state-of-origin round and will beat the Crows who had a number of players involved for South Australia last weekend.
Essendon are the only team to have beaten Port Adelaide at Football Park this year. Don't expect Fremantle to be the second when both teams meet on Saturday night.
The Dockers are competitive and will be strengthened by the return of captain Peter Mann but will be no match for the Power, who should win easily.
HAWKS AND DEMONS
Merger candidates Hawthorn and Melbourne meet at Waverley Park on Sunday.

Sydney-based fullback Chris Langford makes his eagerly awaited return for the Hawks and looks the perfect replacement for the injured Mark Graham and the perfect opponent for rehabilitated Demon full forward David Schwarz.
Expect the rampant Hawks to register their fourth straight win and give the struggling Demons hell.
North Melbourne skipper Wayne Carey returns for his 150th game after an 11-week absence for the grand final replay against the Swans in Sydney on Sunday.
Carey dislocated his shoulder in the first round and steps into the fray to shoulder North's premiership defence.
Swans' skipper Paul Kelly also plays his 150th game and is troubled by a shoulder injury but, like Carey, will attack the ball with his usual ferocity.
Despite the Swans' imposing home record, North have the edge in class and should win a close game.
Collingwood, which clings precariously to eighth place after four straight losses, meets Brisbane at the Gabba on Sunday night.
The Pies are cold at the moment and with the Rocca brothers sadly out of touch, will succumb to the Lions who have begun their belated charge toward the final eight.
*Andrew Bartram is a freelance sports writer who will be writing a regular AFL column for Reuters. He can be contacted at cybercafe@ca.com.au
